subject: Re: Aperture Biotech private deploy — egress proxy, local-SSD tiering & archive plan
messages:
From: Samira Qureshi <samira@aperturebio.com>

Cc: Aperture Biotech IT <it@aperturebio.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private deploy: egress proxy & local-SSD tiering — high-level ask

Hi Michael,

Thanks for taking this. We're in the early stages of scoping a private Redwood deployment in our on-prem colo (Northern CA). A few constraints up front: no outbound model weights may go directly to public cloud storage without encryption+audited transfer; all egress must pass through our corporate HTTP proxy, and we have an on-prem S3-compatible object store (MinIO cluster) reachable over an internal VLAN.

What we'd like Redwood to validate/suggest:
- Recommended approach for egress/proxy configuration so runtime can pull model shards and still satisfy our mTLS and HTTP proxy rules.
- Local-SSD tiering for model KV-cache (NVMe) vs persistent blockstore for canonical model artifacts. How do you recommend evicting or archiving cached local content?
- A graceful archive plan: when a model is updated, how do we persist older weights to object-store and free local SSD without impacting live inference?
- Any required changes to our firewall/NAT config, and whether a dedicated NAT gateway is needed for model pulls.

Attached is our site-inventory.xlsx (rack-level network and storage layout). Can you outline a short mutual action plan and what artifacts Redwood would deliver (network diagram, nodeclass sizing, PV class recommendations, runbook items)?

We'd like to lock a 90-minute workshop next week to walk through the diagram and constraints. Proposed attendees: myself, Jordan (IT), storage engineer, and our compliance lead.

Thanks — Samira
Samira Qureshi
Head of Platform Engineering
Aperture Biotech

Samira — appreciate the clear constraints and the inventory sheet. Quick read-through: this is doable but there are three things we need to validate before we propose exact node counts:

1) Object-store connectivity: is MinIO reachable only from inside the VLAN, or can we route selective egress through your NAT for uploads to an external archival location?
2) KMS/HSM: do you plan to host keys on-prem (HSM) or allow Redwood to manage envelope keys via a customer-managed KMS endpoint? On-prem KMS adds a couple of architecture constraints but is fully supported.
3) Latency/SLO expectations for cold loads from object-store vs warm cache (P50/P95).

Proposed deliverables from Redwood for the workshop:
- Diagram: VPC/VLAN layout, egress flows (proxy + optional NAT gateway), and required firewall ports.
- Nodeclass sizing: control plane, infra, inference (gpu), cache-only local-ssd machines, and archive workers.
- PV class recommendations and eviction/TTL policy for local-SSD cache.
- Runbook snippets: cache flush, model promotion, emergency rollback, and audit steps for transfers.
- Short MA P (mutual action plan) with milestones and owners.

I've attached a short initial-ops-checklist that we use for site preflight. If you can confirm the three points above and availability for the workshop (Wed/Thu next week), we'll draft the diagram first-pass.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Hi Samira / team,

Following Michael's note I sketched a recommended baseline for the on-prem cluster and storage behaviors. This is aimed at minimizing risk, keeping warm model caches as local SSD (fast NVMe), and ensuring auditable archive to MinIO without direct public egress. High-level:

Cluster footprint (baseline for initial rollout):
- Control plane: 3 x m4.large-ish (HA etcd and control components) on management VLAN (no GPU).
- Inference (gpu): 4 x GPU nodes (A5000-class equivalence) dedicated to low-latency traffic.
- Cache-only local SSD nodes: 3 x storage-optimized nodes with 6 x 2TB NVMe per host presented as local PVs for model KV caches.
- Archive workers: 2 x 8vCPU, 32GB RAM nodes (batch transfer workers to push/pull model artifacts to MinIO).

Storage & PV classes:
- local-ssd (local PV, low-latency): hostPath/local-volume via Kubernetes Local Persistent Volume for model KV cache. Mount as read-only for runtime and managed by an eviction controller.
- blockstore (persistent, replicated): on top of your SAN/NAS for canonical model artifacts; used for model persistence before archive.
- archive (object-store): MinIO endpoint; archive workers push model tarballs over internal network using TLS and signed upload tokens.

Cache lifecycle & eviction:
- Cache TTL: 6 hours default for model shards with LRU eviction. Use a small background job that tracks last-access; when total local SSD utilization exceeds 75% trigger targeted eviction of least-recently-used shards.
- Model update/rotation: new model versions are staged into blockstore; cache warmers prefetch into local-ssd during low-traffic windows; post-warm validation flips traffic via feature flag.
- Archive flow: when a model is deprecated, archive worker packages weights, uploads to MinIO with a signed manifest, then signals archive-complete. Post-archive, a node-level cleanup job reclaims local-ssd. All uploads produce audit events with checksum and transfer ID.

Network & egress:
- All outbound HTTP(S) to external endpoints must go through your corporate proxy (10.8.0.2:3128). Configure cluster egress rules and environment variables (HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY) for archive workers and model-pull sidecars.
- For model pulls from third-party repos (if any), use a dedicated NAT gateway that the proxy can route through; this keeps model downloads isolated and auditable.
- Firewall: allow TLS to MinIO nodes on internal ports (TLS 443 equivalent) and restrict control-plane API to management VLAN.

Security & compliance notes:
- Use mutual TLS for node-to-control-plane connections.
- Integrate with your HSM for key wrapping if you will not permit cloud-managed keys. We support signing uploads with a customer-managed KMS endpoint.
- Audit logs: ensure archive workers push transfer logs to your SIEM (we can call a webhook).

Operational runbook excerpts:
- Cold-cache recovery: if local-ssd nodes reboot, archive worker should rehydrate top-n models based on traffic forecasts.
- Emergency rollback: traffic switch controlled by feature flag in the Redwood routing policy; if rollback needed, mark new model as deprecated and warm previous version.

Open questions for the workshop:
- Can MinIO accept multipart uploads from the archive workers (yes/no)?
- Is there an existing service account pattern you prefer for long-lived archive uploads?
- Any hard limits on local NVMe retention (regulatory or ops)?

I'll draft a network diagram (v1) and a short MA P for the next step.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — Michael and Irene. This is exactly the level of detail we were hoping for. A few quick points before the workshop:

- MinIO supports multipart uploads and we can issue service accounts for the archive workers (Jordan will confirm the token TTL).
- KMS: we'll host an on-prem HSM and expose a customer KMS endpoint to Redwood; compliance requires zero-key-exposure to outside parties.
- Retention: regs require model archives kept for 2 years — we need secure immutable storage and retention tags.

Workshop: Thursday 2026-11-25 at 10:00 PT works for us. Agenda: 1) Review v1 network diagram, 2) Approve nodeclass sizes and NVMe placement, 3) Confirm egress NAT/proxy config and firewall rule list, 4) Agree MA P and timeline (2-week sprint to delivery of runbook + diagram).

Can you send the MA P stub and the diagram link ahead of time? Also, please include an estimated infra BOM (order-of-magnitude) for the node types you've suggested so we can route procurement early.

Best — Samira
